scope: AUDIT ONLY. Nothing trained, nothing merged into EyeCU, no EyeCU split touched, no detector or tracker changed, no TEST performance accessed, no further download initiated.
headline: The MOT component did not download. mot-20260811T095052Z-1-001.zip is 158 bytes and contains one empty directory entry. Every MOT question below is therefore UNANSWERABLE from this download, not answered negatively.
GSR contains ZERO ball annotations and ZERO referee annotations -- in all 20 downloaded halves. The categories list declares both; the instance count for both is 0.

GSR bbox_image is a geometry-derived box, not an annotated person box. Height takes 13 distinct values across 38,261 sampled boxes, varies by under 2 px for a single player across a whole half, correlates +0.98 with image row, and 99.1% of boxes are WIDER THAN TALL.

The images the boxes refer to are not in the download. GSR declares 3840x1504 frames in an 'img1' folder; the only pixels downloaded are a 4096x1080 panorama MP4, a different rendering with a different aspect ratio.
The calibration package is the real asset: complete, self-consistent and verified to 8.6 px / 0.83 m.

GSR.schema: SoccerNet-GSR v1.3 JSON: info / images / annotations / categories
GSR.frame_semantics: images 000001..seq_length, 25 fps, image_id = video_id + zero-padded frame

MOT.consequence: no MOT sequence, frame, box, identity, FPS, resolution or class semantics can be reported

BAS.schema: {match_id, fps, actions[{gameTime, label, position, team, player_id}]}

RAW.note: the copy under gsr/ is byte-identical to the copy under raw/ (sha256 933b6d12ef2694a8..., 5799f216ebb688f9...)

identifiers_linking_components.match_id: 128058 -- appears in every RAW filename, the BAS json, the metadata XML and the GSR filename
identifiers_linking_components.player_id: GSR annotations[].attributes.player_id == BAS actions[].player_id == metadata <player id> == player_nodes.csv player_id. This is the join key and it is consistent.
identifiers_linking_components.track_id: GSR-internal, 1..23 for this half. It does NOT appear in BAS, RAW or metadata; it is joined to a real person only through attributes.player_id in the same annotation.
identifiers_linking_components.time: BAS 'position' is milliseconds of match time; metadata <period frameStart/frameEnd/fps> maps match time to recording frames; padding_info.csv gives the ms offset of each half inside the recording.

video_alignment.verdict: NOT ESTABLISHED for bbox_image; ESTABLISHED for pitch coordinates
evidence: GSR declares 3840x1504; the video is 4096x1080. The per-axis ratios differ (1.0667 vs 0.7181), so the GSR image is not this video rescaled.
Naively rescaling bbox_image per axis onto the video puts the boxes in the treeline behind the pitch -- rendered as align_128058_f1200_zoom.jpg.
An offset search over +/-500 frames scored bbox_image placement essentially flat (spread 0.006-0.022), i.e. no temporal alignment was found by that route.
The pitch route DOES land: bbox_pitch -> homography -> mapx puts a marker at each player's feet, visible in the same render.
GSR seq_length 69251 vs 68975 video frames -- 276 frames apart, unexplained by anything in the download.
video_alignment.consequence: This download cannot produce (image, box) training pairs. It can produce (video frame, pitch position) pairs.

human_detector_utility.verdict: NOT USABLE AS DETECTOR GROUND TRUTH

box_tightness_evidence.reading: A standing human is taller than wide at every scale, and a real annotation changes as the player runs, turns and jumps. These boxes do neither: height is a smooth function of position alone. They are synthesised from the calibration, not drawn on the person.

real_player_scale_for_comparison.method: 1.8 m vertical segment projected with the verified fisheye camera model over 1122 pitch positions
real_player_scale_for_comparison.note: real players are 35-161 px tall in the video; the GSR boxes are 37 px tall in a differently scaled space and near-square. The two do not describe the same object.

human_detector_utility.role_assignment_ambiguity: none -- roles are unambiguous where they exist; the problem is the boxes, not the labels
human_detector_utility.small_distant_humans: none below 35 px in the panorama; this is not small-object data

ball_localization_finding.statement: SoccerTrack v2, as downloaded, provides NO ball bounding boxes and NO ball image coordinates.
evidence: GSR declares category id 4 'ball' and contains 0 ball annotations across all 20 halves.
BAS: 23,663 events across 10 matches, 0 of which carry any spatial field. 'position' is a millisecond timestamp, not a place. BAS event labels do NOT imply ball localization.

RAW *_tracker_box_data.xml -- despite the filename -- contains no boxes. It carries per-frame <player loc='[x,y]' speed> and one <ball playerId='ball' loc='[x,y]' speed='NA'/> in NORMALISED PITCH coordinates.

the_one_ball_signal_that_exists.where: RAW *_tracker_box_data.xml <ball> element, per frame at 25 fps
the_one_ball_signal_that_exists.what: a ground-plane pitch position, normalised 0-1, with ballStatus (e.g. BALLOUT) on the frame
the_one_ball_signal_that_exists.why_it_is_not_a_ball_box: It is a pitch-plane point for an object that spends much of the match in the air. Projecting it through the ground homography puts an airborne ball on the grass beneath itself. It also has no extent, so no box can be derived without inventing a radius.
the_one_ball_signal_that_exists.verdict: NOT suitable for ball detector training. Usable at most as a weak temporal prior about where on the pitch the ball is.

bas_utility.timestamp_semantics: 'position' = milliseconds of match time; 'gameTime' = '<period> - M:SS'. Both are times, neither is a place.
bas_utility.temporal_alignment_to_video: POSSIBLE: padding_info.csv gives each half's ms offset and metadata <period frameStart fps> gives the frame mapping, so an event's ms can be turned into a video frame for the one downloaded match.

raw_calibration_finding.verdict: COMPLETE AND VERIFIED -- pixel <-> metre mapping is available for all 10 matches

components_present_per_match.camera_intrinsics.npz: K, D (4-coefficient fisheye), Knew, rvecs, tvecs, rms
components_present_per_match.mapx.npy / mapy.npy: cv2 fixed-point remap, undistorted canvas -> source video pixel
components_present_per_match.keypoints.json: 65 correspondences, key '(x,y)' in pitch METRES -> [u,v] in video pixels
components_present_per_match.padding_info.csv: per-period ms padding and match-time window

raw_calibration_finding.verified_transform_chain: pitch metres --H--> undistorted canvas --mapx--> video pixel

accuracy_128058.note: the two routes come from different files and agree, which is the strongest internal-consistency evidence available

caveats: 132831 has a calibration rms of 1260.95 and an outlying homography. Treat that match's calibration as unusable without re-solving it.
132831 and 132877 have no frameStart/frameEnd in their metadata, so their frame-to-time mapping is missing.
The fisheye fy estimates are poorly constrained (1667 to 80778 across matches) even where rms is good; the homography, not fy, is what the pitch mapping relies on.

This calibrates a FIXED panoramic rig. EyeCU's footage pans, zooms and cuts, so a single per-match homography does not transfer. The value is methodological and as a ground-truth testbed, not as a drop-in.

domain_diversity.competition_level: Japanese university and local amateur football
domain_diversity.team_concentration: 8 of 10 matches involve a University of Tsukuba side (B, B1, B2, C1, C3, Football Society, Medical Soccer Club). Non-Tsukuba opponents: Matsudo City FC, Sakushin Gakuin University, TSC, Chuo Gakuin University.

domain_diversity.camera_geometry: 8 of 10 matches share a 4096x1080 canvas with fx ~1600 and near-identical distortion, i.e. one rig. 117092 (3840x1906, fx 1365) and 132831 (3840x1504) differ.
domain_diversity.lighting: daylight in the downloaded match; not assessable for the others
domain_diversity.camera_motion: none -- fixed panoramic rig, no pan, no zoom, no cuts
domain_diversity.shot_types: one: full-pitch wide. No close-ups, no medium shots, no replays, no graphics.
domain_diversity.comparison_with_eyecu_train: EyeCU TRAIN is 823 images from 29 matches across pro / women / youth / amateur broadcast footage with cuts, zooms, close-ups and replays. SoccerTrack adds volume in a domain EyeCU does not deploy in, and adds none of the shot variety EyeCU actually fails on.

eyecu_leakage_check.method: 500 frames sampled evenly across both downloaded halves, letterbox-stripped 64x64 signature, 8 dihedral orientations, hamming <= 10 then NCC >= 0.95
eyecu_leakage_check.same_source_footage: none -- a fixed panoramic rig over a Japanese university pitch against EyeCU's broadcast and amateur sources
eyecu_leakage_check.test_handling: TEST images were hashed only. No TEST label was opened and nothing was evaluated.

That claim is NOT corroborated by anything in this download and is not restated here as fact. No legal conclusion is drawn beyond what the files contain, which is nothing.

A_player_detector_value.evidence: The annotated images are not in the download, and the boxes are geometry-derived rather than person-shaped (99.1% wider than tall, 13 distinct heights, per-track height std under 2 px across a whole half). Zero usable player boxes.

B_role_classification_value.evidence: Roles are unambiguous and perfectly stable -- 0 role changes across 23 tracks -- and goalkeeper volume is enormous (2.77 M annotations). But there are ZERO referee annotations in all 20 halves, and the role labels are attached to boxes that cannot be used. EyeCU needs referee most of all.

C_identity_tracking_value.evidence: 23 persistent identities per half with no role, jersey or team drift. But every track has a box in every frame: there are no occlusion gaps and no re-entries, so it does not exercise what a tracker must solve. The MOT component that would have been the tracking benchmark is empty. EyeCU already has its own human-verified 900-frame identity benchmark.

D_ball_detector_value.evidence: Zero ball boxes and zero ball image coordinates anywhere. The only ball signal is a per-frame ground-plane pitch point for an object that is frequently airborne. This is the goal EyeCU cares about most and SoccerTrack cannot serve it.

E_event_detection_value.evidence: 23,663 events, 12 classes, ms timestamps, player_id on 99.5%, alignable to video through padding_info and the period frame mapping. Genuinely good data -- for a task EyeCU does not have.

F_jersey_team_player_page_value.evidence: jersey, team side and player_id on every annotation, joined to squad metadata with names, shirt numbers and positions including GK. A complete player-identity graph. Reading a jersey from pixels still needs the img1 frames, which were not downloaded.

G_pitch_calibration_homography_value.evidence: A complete calibration for all 10 matches -- homography, fisheye intrinsics and extrinsics, undistortion maps, 65 pitch correspondences, period padding -- verified end to end at 8.6 px / 0.83 m by two independent routes that agree to 9.8 px. This is the one component that speaks directly to EyeCU's uncalibrated speed and distance, as a worked reference and a ground-truth testbed.

should_we_download_more.reason: The questions that would justify 6.7 GB per additional match are already answered, and answered no: there are no ball boxes, no referee annotations, and no usable person boxes anywhere in SoccerTrack v2. More video is more pixels for annotations that cannot be attached to them. The one high-value component -- calibration -- is already downloaded in full for all ten matches, because it is small and lives in RAW.

single_exception.why: mot-20260811T095052Z-1-001.zip is 158 bytes and empty, so the entire MOT audit is unanswered rather than answered. It is small, and it is the only component that could still overturn the 'no usable boxes' finding.
single_exception.size: unknown, but MOT ground truth is text and is orders of magnitude smaller than a video

explicitly_not_recommended: the remaining nine matches' videos (~60 GB) -- they add one venue, one rig and one shot type
any further GSR halves -- 55 GB is already downloaded and the schema is uniform across all 20

recommended_next_action: Re-fetch the empty MOT archive and re-run this audit's MOT section, since it is small and is the only remaining way SoccerTrack could supply usable boxes. Independently of that, keep the RAW calibration package: it is the strongest external asset found in either audit, and it is the natural reference against which to build and validate EyeCU's pitch calibration -- which is the outstanding blocker behind the UNCALIBRATED speed and distance figures. Do not plan any SoccerTrack-based detector experiment.
